r.정치 구도: In December 2024 a rebel coalition entered Damascus, ending more than 50 years of rule by the Assad family. In March 2025 the transitional government issued an interim constitution that sets a five-year transition and gives the president broad powers. Parliament is a transitional body made up of members chosen by regional electoral colleges and members appointed by the president, not by direct election. The new leadership began as an Islamist armed group, so its biggest test is whether it can include minorities such as Alawites, Druze, Kurds and Christians. In 2025 bloody clashes in Alawite areas on the western coast and Druze areas in the south killed many civilians. The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, which had run the northeast, were folded into state institutions in 2026 and dissolved as a separate army.

t.why: Bordering the Mediterranean, Turkey, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon and Israel, Syria sat at the center of the Middle East's power struggles. During the civil war, Russia and Iran propped up the Assad government, while Turkey and the United States backed different rebel forces. The fall of the government cut the route Iran used to send weapons to Hezbollah in Lebanon, and Russia had to negotiate the future of its Mediterranean naval base with the new authorities. Right after the collapse, Israel moved troops into the buffer zone created by a 1974 ceasefire agreement and took over parts of the south. Millions fled abroad during the war, shaking refugee policy in Turkey, Lebanon, Jordan and Europe. Since the United States and Europe lifted most sanctions in 2025, the new questions are who will pay for reconstruction and which countries will gain influence.
t.rel: Civil war began in 2011, and the Assad regime fell in December 2024. The new government is widening ties with the West and the Gulf states, while Israel occupies parts of the south and the Golan Heights.
t.korea: South Korea established diplomatic relations with Syria in April 2025, completing ties with every UN member except North Korea. Under the Assad government, Syria had been close to North Korea since establishing relations in 1966, and North Korea was suspected of helping Syria build a nuclear reactor. Four months after the change of government, South Korea's foreign minister traveled to Damascus to sign the joint statement establishing relations. South Korea pledged humanitarian aid such as medicine, medical equipment and rice. Syria hopes South Korea will help get sanctions fully lifted and take part in reconstruction.
t.know: Damascus is counted among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
etext: Nearly 14 years of civil war badly damaged cities, the power grid, roads and factories. The World Bank put the cost of reconstruction at more than $200 billion, close to ten times the size of the economy in 2024.

Before the war, oil from the northeast along with wheat and cotton kept the state afloat. With the Kurdish-led forces that long held the oil region merging into the state in 2026, reviving oil output has become key to reconstruction.

Since the United States and Europe lifted most sanctions in 2025, international banking and foreign investment have become possible again. Companies from the Gulf, Turkey and Europe are moving into power plants, ports and airports.

The currency has lost much of its value and most people live in poverty. Many places get electricity for only a few hours a day, and many skilled workers have left the country. Renewed insecurity could easily stall investment.
